title: Integral Brown criterion and obstruction in categorical Ext groups
statement: Let ℓ be prime, E a finite intermediate extension of Q_ℓ with condensed valuation ring Λ [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring], and X a separated finite-type scheme over a field k of characteristic p>0 different from ℓ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let Cons(X,Λ) denote the constant-model constructible sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Then BrownHypothesesFor Λ X [lem-sfb-brown-hypotheses-criterion] holds if and only if for each C in Cons(X,Λ) there exists d in ℕ such that Ext^q(C,N) [def-pc-ext] is zero for every N in Cons(X,Λ) and q≥d. The bound can depend on C but is uniform in N. Consequently, if some C has nonzero Ext^q(C,N) for arbitrarily large natural q, with N allowed to depend on q, the Brown bundle is false. The HasExt infrastructure fixes Ext in universe u+1; it is available from the existing derived category and adds no vanishing hypothesis. No finiteness of the field cohomological dimension is asserted.

source.place: paragraph 2, integral compactness; explicit Ext-bound hypothesis of sk-prop-int-compactness-compact

proof.text: Apply the proved integral Brown criterion. It gives equivalence with a bound d in ℤ on the ambient Hom(C[0],N[0][q]), uniform over constructible N. Every integral and geometric hypothesis of that criterion is retained.

Mathlib Abelian.Ext.homEquiv identifies natural-degree categorical Ext with these ambient shifted Hom groups, so subsingletonness transports in both directions. Given the integer bound d use d.toNat+1 as a natural inclusive bound. Conversely, a natural inclusive bound d gives integer strict bound d, because q>d≥0 can be lifted to ℕ. Thus no negative-degree case is omitted.

For the obstruction, apply the forward criterion to the fixed source C. Choose a target N, a degree q at least its resulting bound, and a nonzero Ext class from the unboundedness hypothesis. The criterion makes that group subsingleton; the class equals zero, a contradiction.

proof_origin.note: A proved Ext API for the supported conditional criterion. Does not prove or assume the disputed arbitrary-field brownHypotheses theorem, and does not add any unproved statement.

lean.statement:
theorem brownHypothesesFor_padicIntegers_iff_categorical_ext_bounded
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p) (hpℓ : p ≠ ℓ)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E) X))] :
    BrownHypothesesFor (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E) X ↔
      ∀ C : ConstantModelConstructible (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E) X,
        ∃ d : ℕ,
          ∀ N : ConstantModelConstructible (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E) X,
            ∀ q : ℕ, d ≤ q → Subsingleton (Abelian.Ext.{u + 1} C.obj N.obj q)

edge_cases: The argument allows empty schemes, zero sheaves, zero Ext groups and negative integer bounds. The inclusive natural bound is d.toNat+1, not d.toNat, in the forward direction. The obstruction requires arbitrarily large degrees, so a single nonzero degree-zero group does not refute Brown. No choice of data from an unproved existence theorem occurs.
